paragraph: Closter is a single-family town, with 49 detached sales over six months at a median of $1,338,000, and the typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths, though split-levels and bi-levels make up a real share of the volume. Sales ran from $670,000 to $4,288,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. A sale-to-list ratio of 1.00 with 45 percent of homes going above asking and a median of 17 days on market says competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes move quickly here, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Volume built the way it normally does, from three closings in February to 13, 11, and 14 in May through July, and medians firmed over those same months rather than softening, so the town is tracking the seasonal arc with strength on the price side. If Closter follows the usual pattern, expect volume to taper modestly through fall before deep winter thins it out. The condo and townhouse side is barely a market: four townhouse sales, all at $1,500,000, all closing in June. That is too small a sample to read as a trend, but it tells you attached product here competes at single-family prices, not below them. If you're comparing the two, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
